headline: The First Woman to Swim the English Channel
meta_description: 100 years ago, Gertrude Ederle became the first woman to cross the English Channel, beating the fastest male time by nearly 2 hours.
summary_short: A century ago today, Olympic champion Gertrude Ederle swam the English Channel in 14 hours 34 minutes—faster than any man had done before.
body:
One hundred years ago today, American swimmer Gertrude Ederle achieved what no woman had done before: she crossed the English Channel. Starting at Cap Gris-Nez in France at 07:08 am on August 6th, 1926, the Olympic gold medalist completed the crossing in 14 hours and 34 minutes, beating the fastest male channel-swimming time by nearly 2 hours. Stormy conditions pushed her beyond her intended landing point, forcing her to swim the equivalent of 35 miles before finally reaching shore at Kingsdown, Kent. An exhausted, waterlogged teenager greeted the first person on land—a British immigration officer who immediately asked for her passport.

Ederle's achievement came after a lifetime of breaking records. Called "The Queen of the Waves," she had already captured Olympic gold and held world records in five swimming events, earning a ticker-tape parade through New York City after competing in Paris in 1924. When the Women's Swimming Association sponsored her and fellow swimmer Helen Wainwright to attempt the Channel crossing in 1925, Wainwright was forced to withdraw due to injury. Rather than wait, Ederle decided to pursue the dream alone. Her first attempt, made approximately one year earlier, had been disqualified. This time, with contracts from both the New York Daily News and Chicago Tribune funding her training expenses and providing a modest salary, she succeeded.

Ederle's legacy endured long after that August morning. She was inducted into the International Swimming Hall of Fame as an "Honor Swimmer" in 1965, and later honored with induction into the National Women's Hall of Fame in 2003. Her Channel crossing remains one of sport's defining moments—a testament to determination, skill, and the refusal to accept limits.
quick_facts: Gertrude Ederle crossed the English Channel on August 6, 1926
Completed the 35-mile swim in 14 hours and 34 minutes
Beat the fastest male crossing time by nearly 2 hours
Olympic gold medalist and five-time world record holder
First woman ever to swim the English Channel
